title: The most expensive mistake is a same-day flight.
subtitle: Every missed-embarkation story I've handled started at an airport, not a gangway.

kicker: Why the ship cannot help you
text: A ship will not wait for a delayed flight.
sub: Departure slots are set by port authority scheduling and maritime requirements — the captain frequently cannot simply hold the ship. The airline's apology does not move it.

title: Three things a day early buys you

items.head: A margin measured in hours
items.body: A cancelled evening flight becomes an inconvenience rather than a forfeited voyage.

items.head: Luggage that catches up
items.body: Delayed bags can be rerouted to a hotel overnight. They cannot chase a ship at sea.

items.head: A rested first evening
items.body: You board unhurried, unpack before dinner, and begin the sailing awake rather than recovering.

title: The flight you book decides the risk

left.label: Same day
items: Bags arrive with you or not

points.label: Weather
points.value: One storm at a connecting hub, and every later flight that day is full.

points.label: Mechanical
points.value: A swapped aircraft can cost you six hours you did not have.

points.label: Connections
points.value: Two flights in one day double the number of things that must go right.

points.label: Cruise air
points.value: Protection varies by line and fare — confirm what yours actually covers.

text: Book the hotel night. It is the cheapest insurance in the itinerary.
sub: And if you are crossing an ocean to meet a ship, treat two nights as the standard rather than the indulgence.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with
body: I'll tell you plainly which of your flights has no margin in it, and what the day-before version of the trip looks like.
